messages:
prod-oncall: :rotating_light: Observed big spike in token-prep CPU on inference-prod-03 around 18:12 UTC. Multiple tokenizer pods OOMKilled in last 3m, some nodes showing kernel OOM kills. Paging oncall.
incident-bot: Incident created PD-4456 and paging @kyle (prod oncall) :pager: — severity: high — affected service: serving/runtime/token-prep.
kyle: I'm awake, looking now. Which pods? any obvious pattern (same node / same image)?
anya: saw a wave of very long prompts from a single client key ~18:10-18:15, lots of regex-heavy preproc. Also seeing `cudaErrorUnknown: 999` in one of the runtime logs.
ellie-cs: any customer-facing errors yet? CS seeing elevated 500s for a small set of enterprise customers. Can we confirm impact and if we need a status update?
prod-oncall: p50 latency for /v1/generate up ~2x, error rate for tokenization path increased from 0.2% -> 8% on that window. Top caller tag: customer:enterprise-xyz (spike of long prompts).
kyle: grabbing pod list... running:
```
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep token
inference-token-prep-7f6c9   0/1  CrashLoopBackOff  3 (OOMKilled)  10m  ip-10-0-12-45
inference-token-prep-5b2a7   1/1  Running           0              5m   ip-10-0-13-11
inference-token-prep-9d1f0   0/1  OOMKilled         2              4m   ip-10-0-12-45
```
kyle: logs show memory alloc failures and rare cuda driver errors:
```
[2026-03-15T18:11:42Z] runtime: out of memory allocating 2147483648 bytes
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
E CudaDriver Error: 999 (cudaErrorUnknown)
[2026-03-15T18:11:43Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 32145 (token-prep) score 987 or sacrifice child
```
anya: looks like the tokenizer preproc is trying to create huge intermediate buffers for pathological inputs. This is CPU/memory (host) OOMs causing the container to be killed; some nodes then show kernel-level OOMs and the GPU driver errors cascade.
prod-oncall: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) throttle/queue requests for long prompts, 2) route traffic away from affected node(s), 3) restart affected pods after enabling a safe memory cap.
kyle: I'm going to set a temporary admission rule to reject prompts > 200k chars and add a soft-length reject for the enterprise tag. Pushing a mitigation patch now.
ops-bot: rolling update triggered: set env TOKEN_PREP_MAX_CHARS=200000 for deployment inference-token-prep (canary first).
kyle: canary rolled to two pods on different nodes. Observing lower memory pressure on the canary. Also created Kubernetes `LimitRange` to cap container memory at 8Gi as temporary safeguard.
anya: also recommend disabling experimental regex-heavy branch for preproc. Pushing a hotfix to skip that code-path when prompt_length > 50k.
infra-led: I'm going to cordon ip-10-0-12-45 (node with repeated kernel OOMs) and drain remaining pods after we stabilize. Please hold on restarts for pods pinned to that node.
prod-oncall: ellie-cs - do we need a customer status? Which customers got 5xxs?
ellie-cs: enterprise-xyz reported failures and CS has opened a support ticket. Suggest a short status note: "We are experiencing elevated errors for some requests due to input preprocessing overload; mitigation in progress." Drafting now.
kyle: after canary looks good, I'm routing traffic for enterprise-xyz to a fallback model endpoint (quantized variant) to reduce memory usage for their requests. Patch applied to routing rule with tag-based override.
ops-bot: routing rule updated: route(customer_tag=enterprise-xyz) -> model: rwd/quant-fallback-v1.
prod-oncall: monitoring: memory pressure dropped by ~70% on affected nodes after caps and routing change. Error rate back down to ~0.6%. Latency returning toward normal.
anya: we should also add a regex time-limit and defensively tokenize in chunks to avoid huge allocations. Filing a follow-up ticket to harden preproc.
infra-led: node ip-10-0-12-45 drained and cordoned; kernel OOM process being investigated (possible sysctl vm.overcommit tuning). Will keep node offline until we confirm stability.
ellie-cs: posted customer status update and notified enterprise-xyz that we've routed them to a fallback and are investigating root cause.
prod-oncall: creating incident timeline + actions, will handoff to infra for postmortem. Thanks team — mitigation successful for now.
incident-bot: PD-4456 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity downgraded to low. Postmortem task assigned to kyle and anya.
infra-led: taking handoff for root cause analysis and follow-up on node config / kernel OOMs. ping me if you need deeper host logs (I will keep node offline until clear).
prod-oncall: final note: probable immediate cause = pathological prompt set causing massive tokenization allocations; contributing factor = lack of memory caps in token-prep container + fallback routing not enabled. Follow-ups: add mem limits, prompt length enforcement at gateway, chunked tokenization, and expanded e2e test with pathological prompts.
kyle: acknowledged — will work on the postmortem and schedule follow-up fixes.
ellie-cs: dropping a link to the support ticket and customer contact for the postmortem.
prod-oncall: closing oncall thread — moving to postmortem. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
